publication_metadata.title: Failure of strong quadratic growth in unregularized sparse control of a critical wave equation
publication_metadata.description: We give an explicit negative answer to retaining ordinary critical-cone strict positivity and strong control-L2 quadratic growth after removing quadratic control regularization from the Kunisch–Meinlschmidt energy-critical quintic-wave model. On the three-dimensional unit ball, zero is the unique global optimizer for a sufficiently small positive pointwise Hilbert control cap. Its ordinary critical cone is zero and the strict condition is vacuous, while feasible controls converging in L-infinity have objective gap o(||u||L2^2). For nearby radial terminal targets, every global optimizer has L2 displacement divided by target displacement tending to infinity. Local L1 quadratic growth survives, with fixed-basepoint weaker-norm bounds. Every fixed finite nonnegative terminal-velocity weight is allowed; the radial lower comparison neighborhood may depend on that weight. The verification archive supplies standalone LaTeX, exact control/algebra checkers with full receipt comparisons, analytic derivations, original submission provenance, source pins and bounded priority audits. Classical wave estimates, group-sparse thresholds and concentration/noncoercivity theory are explicitly credited. The result concerns the unchanged strong-L2 implication, not all adapted unregularized sufficient conditions. No worldwide-firstness certificate or sharp-rate theorem is claimed. AI tools were used extensively in construction, derivation, internal independent adversarial verification, computation, literature research and writing. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.
